newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia central bank modifies banks rating rules.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia central bank modifies banks rating rules.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank has modified some rating rules in a move to improve the soundness of the country's more than 200 commercial banks.

The new rules, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters on Tuesday, are effective immediately and include asset quality criteria, management and liquidity, with the focus on the capital adequacy ratios.

However, the overall weighting of the soundness of a bank remains unchanged, with the capital requirement accounting for 25 percent, asset quality 30 percent, management quality 25 percent, earnings 10 percent and liquidity 10 percent.
Those factors are also known as CAMEL ratios. Banks that can meet all the requirements will be given 100 points.

A bank is sound if it can obtain 81 to 100 points from the central bank, while those ranging between 66 to 80, 51 to 65 and nil to 50 points are rated sound enough, less sound and unsound respectively.
The bank said the new rules require banks to have a capital adequacy ratio of eight percent, otherwise they will be classified as less sound.
Banks were given 65 to 79 points in the past with a capital adequacy ratio of between 6.5 and 7.9 percent. The new rules say 7.9 percent will be given only 65 points and rated less sound.
The bank said it also modified one of the two ratios to rate asset quality with the focus on the allowance for loan losses.
It said the liquidity ratio was tightened as well, reducing the loan-to-deposit-ratio to not more than 90 percent to obtain full points from the central bank from a previous 110 percent.
The central bank said management factors were reduced to 100 aspects from 250 earlier, switching the focus to general and risk management from capital, asset, rentability and liquidity.
